summary: Phase 2 (Model C) SKU hierarchy & variant management — full backend regression test suite created and executed (17/17 passing) plus frontend smoke test on Stock Dashboard branding UI. All new endpoints verified: batch target_child_sku_id create/update/clear/invalid-id, batch → warehouse transfer with 3 classification modes (default from batch target, '' → Generic, explicit child), branding entries stock-breakdown/create/list/over-quantity/reverse direction, distributor stock transfer with classification + per-classification availability guard + reverse restores classification-correct quantities on both sides, and legacy regression (plain no-child transfer, warehouse-stock-overview, stock-summary). Test fixtures self-cleanup verified in Mongo (no test data leaked).

minor.issue: Cascade stock rollback finds factory_warehouse_stock via (tenant, warehouse, sku_id) only — does NOT include child_sku_id in the query, so a batch that produced BOTH a Generic and a branded stock row will only roll back one of them. Reference production_qc.py L878-882.

action_items: Consider adding child_sku_id to the force-delete cascade stock rollback query in production_qc.delete_batch so both classifications are cleaned up when a mixed-classification batch is force-deleted (minor).
critical_code_review_comments: Branding entry FIFO logic (branding_entries.py L190-210) uses {'$in': [None]} on child_sku_id when it should be None — this works but is unusual. Same pattern in production_qc.py L2073. Consider using explicit None once the migration is complete.
distributor_stock_transfers.py POST create endpoint (L1145-1157) mutates payload.items to hydrate child_sku_name — fine for this request but consider not mutating request models; use a derived dict.
branding_entries.py _load_location raises 400 for a missing warehouse location — should be 404 for consistency with '_resolve_child' which raises 404.
